name: Billionbrains Garage Ventures Ltd
title: Billionbrains Garage Ventures Ltd - 544603 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Groww Q4 FY26 call is a retail broking platform update with no supply-side capital-cycle content; management guided margin expansion only if revenue grows above 15%, and gave no numeric guidance.

summary.headline: Groww's Q4 FY26 call gave no hard financial figures; equity F&O market share rose to 10.6% from 9.1%, with active derivative customers at about 17 lakh per quarter.
summary.overview: Management's prepared remarks were high-level: FY26 was the first year as a listed company, with new launches in commodities, bonds (secondary), wealth (Fisdom, W, Prime) and an AMC partnership with SSG pending approval. Management said industry activity is still well below the peak, with FIIs negative and March 2026 volatility hitting MTF and commodity accounts. Several data requests (affluent AUM and revenue share, average MTF book, MTF share of cash ADTO, Fisdom and AMC revenue, commodity ADTO share) were deferred to follow-up. Management reiterated that cost to grow is roughly INR 450-500 crore a year and will be kept below revenue growth.

segments.name: Broking (Groww platform)
segments.commentary: Equity and F&O share gains continued; F&O penetration of the customer base is about 10%, versus about 18% before November 2024. ARPU is back to pre-November 2024 levels, driven by MTF and commodities offsetting lower F&O mix.

segments.name: Wealth (Fisdom, W, Prime)
segments.commentary: Fisdom was acquired about six months ago; Prime launched in January 2026. Management said it is too early to comment on scaling or cross-sell. The shareholder letter targets Fisdom profitability by FY28.

segments.name: AMC (SSG partnership)
segments.commentary: Pending regulatory approvals. Management said AMC hiring will add cost, and AMC revenue was not disclosed on the call.

segments.name: Commodities and bonds
segments.commentary: Commodities launched a little over a year ago; commodity ADTO market share will be disclosed after the one-year mark. Bonds secondary market launched after primary.

guidance_outlook: Cost to operate (Groww platform) rises in Q1 FY27 due to a one-time appraisal increase, then stays broadly flat in absolute terms for the rest of the year, excluding risk-related costs.
Cost to serve expected to fall as a share of revenue, though absolute tech and AI costs rise.
Cost to grow expected to rise slightly from INR 450-500 crore but grow more slowly than revenue. Q1 marketing spend is seasonally higher (IPL), and FY27 spend is expected to be slightly above FY26.
Margin expansion depends on revenue growth: management said margins expand above about 15% revenue growth and more so at about 30%; they do not expand at lower growth.
Management expects FY27 to be the inflection point for AI in customer experience and productivity. No algo or API strategy yet, pending regulatory clarity.
capex_capacity: Depreciation rose QoQ, mainly due to the Fisdom acquisition.
Employee cost rose QoQ on investment in AMC, wealth and AI, with headcount at about 1,800.
No capex figures or capacity disclosures were given on the call.
demand_pricing: Industry growth: management cited about 10-15% CAGR over the long run, with step-ups in bull markets. It said the industry is still away from the bottom, with FIIs negative and tariffs weighing on sentiment.
Acquisition funnel has shifted toward mutual funds and ETFs since September 2024. SIPs remain a major source of AUM accumulation.
Customer AUM dipped on an M2M basis in March 2026, but inflows held up as most customers stayed in profit after 31 March. Management said April was better than March.
Stock advisory and MF advisory demand is among the highest voice-of-customer requests; launch timing not set.
Settlement: customers choose bill-to-bill, monthly or quarterly settlement; quarterly is the default most customers prefer.

qa_highlights.question: How have customer cohorts from 2023-24 performed through the market correction, and how does their behaviour differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition has shifted toward MF and ETF; SIP flows continue. Most customers are still profitable, and the March dip was mainly M2M. No cohort-level AUM data was given.

qa_highlights.question: Equity F&O market share jumped to 10.6% from 9.1%. What drove it, and what is the algo share?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers were new customers, initiatives including 915, and higher quarterly transacting customers (about 17 lakh vs 14 lakh). Algo and API volumes are not meaningful, and there is no algo strategy yet.

qa_highlights.question: Did employee cost and depreciation rise because of Fisdom, and will this continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation rose mainly due to Fisdom. Employee cost rose on investment in AMC, wealth and AI. Headcount is about 1,800.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MTF customer profile and what is the average MTF book?
qa_highlights.answer: No study was done. MTF is mostly used by existing customers, not as an acquisition product. The average book will be disclosed later, and the peak was around end-January or February.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook and the cost to acquire customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin expansion depends on revenue growth, with about 15% as a threshold. Cost to grow is largely acquisition spend, is roughly fixed on an annual basis, and Q1 is seasonally higher.

qa_highlights.question: Industry active clients have plateaued near 50 million. What supports growth, and are there open interest limits or settlement changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth depends on bull markets; long-run industry CAGR is about 10-15%. Open interest is under half the limit on average and was not hit in Q4. Quarterly settlement is customer choice, not a regulatory mandate.

risks_watch: Market volatility: March 2026 negative balances and M2M losses in MTF and commodities were booked as risk-related cost to operate.
Regulatory risk on F&O and speculation curbs; management said it engages regulators at industry level.
Fisdom and wealth investment needs and FY28 profitability target; wealth scale-up is still early.
Pending SSG AMC approvals and AMC integration costs.
Undisclosed data: affluent AUM and revenue share, Fisdom and AMC revenue, average MTF book, commodity ADTO share, and the market-share methodology change.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core broking franchise and share gains, but evasive on wealth scaling, algo strategy and several data requests, which were deferred. Management was cautious on the market, saying the industry is still away from the bottom.
key_quotes: So the customer might not be doing derivatives in last quarter but started doing derivatives in this quarter, might be doing stocks or mutual fund in the last quarter.
But what we have seen is at an aggregate level , most of these customers are still profitable with obviously 31st March being not a best day for cut off
We keep on saying that if our revenue grows beyond let's say 15% th en probably the margin will keep on expanding.
And the second on the algo side, I think we don't have, it's not meaningful. Any API or algo today is not really meaningful in terms of any transactions.

growth.why: No hard revenue or EBITDA guidance was given; management only guided cost to grow at INR 450-500 crore (broadly flat) and said margins expand only if revenue grows above ~15%, with backing limited to equity F&O share gains (10.6% from 9.1%) and new launches still pending approval, so growth support is vague.
